activities.caption: file each element under its covenant
activities.name: judCovenantSort

config.prompt: Abraham, Sinai, David — file each element:

items.label: Genesis 12 and 17 — 'I will make of you a great nation'
sealed by circumcision; election as vocation, not privilege
the whole people, freed from Egypt, accepts the Torah at the mountain
the 613 mitzvot of rabbinic counting are its terms
the midrash imagines every nation offered it first, each declining
its broken appearance drives the messianic hope

config.why: Sinai is the decisive one; chosenness functions inside the tradition as assignment of duty ('a light unto the nations'), not superiority — and the tradition's own texts argue both directions, as usual.

activities.caption: the oven of Akhnai — you are one of the rabbis
activities.name: judAkhnaiBranch

config.root: A rabbi's ruling has been outvoted by his colleagues. He calls on heaven to validate it — and a carob tree uproots itself, a stream flows backward, a divine voice confirms him. You sit in the study house. What do you rule?

start.text: The miracles and the voice are before you. Do they settle the case?

choices.label: Accept heaven's vote
choices.feedback: Understood — but the rabbis overrule God Himself: 'It is not in heaven' (Deuteronomy 30:12); the Torah was given to humans to interpret.

choices.label: Overrule — the Torah is not in heaven
choices.feedback: The majority holds — and God, the story ends, laughed: 'My children have defeated me.'

heaven-rules.text: A tidy outcome — but it would end the argument, and the argument is the point: majority and minority views are both preserved on the Talmud's pages.

rabbis-rule.text: Study itself becomes worship; argument becomes devotion — 'these and these are the words of the living God'.

config.why: Interpretation is the tradition's main event: midrash mines narrative gaps, the PaRDeS layers name the senses, and halakhah ('the way one walks') applies the texts to every domain — kashrut, Sabbath, family, commerce.

activities.anchor: in some tellings, the reason the world was created
activities.caption: true or false — Torah vs law code
activities.name: judTorahJudge

statements.s: 'Torah' means teaching — narrative, argument and relationship, not merely a law code.
statements.why: The Five Books of Moses, hand-written on parchment scrolls and read through the annual cycle, plus the oral Torah beside them.

statements.s: Halakhah is mechanical rule-following, fixed once and for all.
statements.why: Halakhah ('the way one walks') is case-law reasoning in a two-millennia debate — majority and minority views preserved on the same pages.

statements.s: The Mishnah (c. 200 CE) and the Talmud (c. 500 CE) carry the oral Torah.
statements.why: Compiled after the Temple's destruction — commentary upon commentary, the multi-generational discussion.

statements.s: Study of the argument itself is treated as a form of worship.
statements.why: In some tellings, the very reason for creation — which is why a portable book could become the tradition's centre.

activities.anchor: The arc that the texts and the archaeology jointly sketch
activities.caption: scrub the arc — temple to text to diaspora
activities.name: judArcTimeline

events.title: Merneptah Stele
events.text: The first extra-biblical mention of 'Israel' — an Egyptian victory inscription.

events.title: First Temple destroyed
events.text: The Babylonian exile — from which Judaism returned edited, monotheised and textual.

events.title: Second Temple period
events.text: 516 BCE–70 CE: Greek conquest, the Maccabean revolt (the Chanukah story), Roman rule, the sects the Dead Sea Scrolls illuminate.

events.title: The Temple falls — rabbinic Judaism rises
events.text: Rome ends the sacrificial religion; the rebuild at Yavneh centres on text, prayer and law — portable because its centre is a book.

events.title: The expulsion from Spain
events.text: Ends the Sephardi golden age of Hebrew poetry and philosophy under Islam.

events.title: The state of Israel
events.text: Changes the tradition's demography and its theology's problems — after the Holocaust murdered six million, two-thirds of European Jewry.

activities.anchor: refuses to be defined by them
activities.caption: drag between the thread and the creations
activities.name: judThreadCompare

config.prompt: Two millennia, two ledgers — drag the divider:

before.label: What was done
before.text: The thread: early supersessionism, medieval expulsions (England 1290, France 1306, Spain 1492), ghettoisation, blood-libel, the pogroms of the Russian Empire, the industrialised murder of the Holocaust.

after.label: What was produced
after.text: The same two millennia: the Talmud, Hebrew poetry, mysticism, Hasidism's revival — and the reinventions of every exile, a text-centred portable peoplehood.

config.why: The study includes the persecutions; the account the tradition gives of itself keeps its own centre of gravity — survival through adaptation, arguably one of history's most successful survival strategies.

activities.caption: pair each stream with where it locates authority
activities.name: judStreamsMatch

config.prompt: One people, many streams — pair each with its stance:

pairs.right: the double Torah is revealed; halakhah binding (modern-Orthodox and stricter Haredi worlds)
historical-critical scholarship accepted — change through law, not against it
personal autonomy in observance — the largest North American stream

config.why: Beneath the denominations runs the peoplehood fact: identity carried by birth as well as belief — a Jew who practises nothing is still, by communal definition, a Jew. The category the tradition uses for itself is a nation with a covenant.
